profile.name: Brian Sawaya
profile.pitch: I design and build robots and medical devices.

bio: I lead AutoLab at Neurotech@Berkeley and take on client projects with Engineering Solutions @ Berkeley.

timeline.title: AutoLab: Neuron Culturing Robot
timeline.impact: Lead a team of 5 building a cell-culture robot with 0.1 mm repeatability.
bullets: Building a multi-axis gantry that moves culturing tools across well plates
Designed the pipette drive with stepper motors and A4988 drivers; now building a mechanical tool changer
Won a $2,000 Jacobs Ignite grant and trained 30+ members in cell culturing
timeline.imageAlt: CAD model of the AutoLab gantry robot over a well plate

gallery.alt: Control interface with camera preview and gantry position
Sterile enclosure concept and first-semester poster

timeline.title: Smart Insole for Diabetic Foot Ulcers
timeline.impact: Insole that flags ulcer risk when left and right feet differ by 2.2 °C.
bullets: Programmed two Arduino Nano 33 IoT boards in C++ to read 4 thermistors per foot and an IMU over I2C
Streamed live sensor data over Bluetooth Low Energy to a Python logger
Owned the data pipeline, the Bluetooth link, and the bill of materials
timeline.imageAlt: System diagram: thermistors and an IMU on each foot feed an Arduino Nano 33 IoT, which sends data over Bluetooth Low Energy to a Python logger

timeline.title: Linear Array Detector for Mass Spectrometry
timeline.org: Engineering Solutions @ Berkeley · Client: Williams Lab, UC Berkeley
timeline.impact: Aligned a 19-hole electrode array to under 0.1 mm between plates.
bullets: Proof of concept for identifying viral infections from vaporized saliva
Located the plates with reamed dowel pin holes, M3 fasteners, and a resin-printed alignment jig
Compared 9 manufacturing methods and reached ~40% ion transmittance against a 60% target
timeline.imageAlt: CAD model of the linear array detector between two mounting plates

gallery.alt: Full mass spectrometer assembly in CAD and the first laser-cut plate prototype
Locating plate iterations, datum block, and film spacer
Electrode stack and linear array sub-assembly

timeline.title: BioMyo: Muscle-Controlled Prosthetic Arm
timeline.impact: Prosthetic arm driven by muscle signals; Voter's Choice out of 160+ projects.
bullets: Led 5 students using Arduino and EMG electrodes to replicate arm motion
Placed 3rd of 20+ teams at a hackathon
Featured at the MIT x Harvard Augmentation Summit
timeline.imageAlt: Live EMG demo of the BioMyo arm at a research symposium
